description: Before becoming the first man to free dive beyond 100 meters, Jacques Mayol was already searching for watches capable of accompanying him on his underwater explorations. This Seamaster Plongeur de Luxe is one of the rare survivors from that pioneering era, when the limits of both man and technology were still being defined. title: Girard Peregaux, Gyromatic Deep Diver MK1 ref 1267
description: This Gyromatic Deep Diver is an exceptionally rare watch. Produced for only a brief period, just a handful of examples are believed to have survived. Yet rarity is only part of its appeal. Its design is truly unique, remarkably avant-garde for its time.  From its applied shark-tooth hour markers to its true alpha-shaped hands, every detail defies convention. And yet, it all works. The design is remarkably well balanced and gracefully harmonious. title: UG Compax 30 chronograph ref 22205
description: Universal Geneve started as a chronograph watch brand. They established the standard of design for elegant chronographs and this almost 90 years «Compax 30 »  is a classic from this era.  The name Compax 30 refers to its distinctive 30-minute chronograph register, rather than the more common 45- or 60-minute counters found on most chronographs of the period. title: Datejust 16013 2 tones gilt dial
description: Probably the most iconic Datejust seen in 80s Hong Kong gangster movies — the Rolex Datejust ref. 16013 in its unmistakable two-tone configuration, here fitted with a gilt glossy black dial.  The watch is, of course, in pristine condition, paired with its signature Jubilee bracelet. The glossy dial is immaculate, exactly as it should be.  It comes complete with its original papers, confirming its provenance from… Hong Kong — where else?

title: The OG Favre Leuba Deep Blue MK1
description: The Favre-Leuba Deep Blue Mk I is one of the most distinctive dive watches of the 1960s. While its aluminum bezel sets it apart from the Mk II that would follow, it is above all its extraordinary asymmetrical dial that defines its character. Dominated by a large luminous crosshair spanning the entire dial, its design is as bold as it is timeless. title: Tropical Polerouter Date
description: Nice tropical Polerouters are hard to find as the white wolf.   Here’s a ref. 204607-1, fully overhauled and featuring an evenly tropicalized dial. A true wabi-sabi Polerouter, where tiny imperfections add depth, charm, and character.  The dial color is simply stunning under the NOS signed plexi. A charismatic Polerouter, a perfect summer watch and the thrill of a genuine tropical Polerouter—without breaking the bank.

title: Chronograph Jardur Bezelmeter 960
description: Here is a 1940’s pilote watch with a unique degrees scale on the dial.  It’s allows the pilot to calculate the duration to achieve a certain degrees turn at a constant degree angle. At 3° per second, the pilot would reach 90° right after the central chronograph hand passed the 30-second mark.  We Love this black glossy dial with the red accents. description: Beautiful Polerouters are becoming increasingly hard to find. Long under the radar, the recent spotlight on the brand has reignited collectors’ enthusiasm for the finest examples.  A true classic among classics, here is a ref. 869111. A 36mm Polerouter date with trapeze date window and original signed crown. The signed plexi reveals a beautifully preserved black glossy dial. title: Seamaster 600 « PloProf » MK4
description: The Seamaster 600, better known as the “PloProf” — short for Plongeur Professionnel — needs little introduction. The ultimate aquatic tool watch, it became legendary through its association with COMEX divers, expeditions aboard Captain Cousteau’s Calypso, and even on the wrist of stylish industrialist Gianni Agnelli, the iconic head of Ferrari. description: Before COMEX shifted its allegiance to Rolex, Henri Delauze was wearing and testing the PloProf alongside Omega’s research team. Although COMEX ultimately chose the Sea-Dweller as its official watch, the PloProf remains one of the most radical dive watches ever made and a true legend of the race for greater depths. description: If you’re looking for an affordable pre-moon Speedmaster with all the vintage feel and DNA, this is probably it. title: 1984 Speedmaster with rare Télémètre bezel
description: From the 1970s through the 1990s, the ref. 145.022 remained remarkably consistent, evolving only subtly over nearly two decades. Sitting right in the middle of this long production run, this 1984 Speedmaster is often regarded as one of the best-value vintage Speedmasters available today. More affordable than a new one, it offers a compelling blend of vintage charm and everyday reliability. description: The rarest of the Sport UG Compax family. Most serious research points to fewer than 300–400 pieces produced per dial color, with probably less than 30 examples known today across both configurations. The white dial 884100/02 stands as the rarer of the two, with only a handful of documented pieces in collector circles.  This example is one of those few survivors. description: Here is an exceptional tropical ’69.  Its nobility comes from its serial number, sitting perfectly within the official “chocolate” range. Being among the early ’69s, it also inherits a DON bezel from the calibre 321 Speedmasters.  And what a bezel it is. Beautifully faded over the years, it now pairs perfectly with the chocolate dial. title: Blancpain Fifty Fathoms Rotomatic Incabloc
description: The Fifty Fathoms is a legend. And this one is an affordable grail. The condition is second to none. A dressy museum grade Blancpain Fifty Fathoms. Sharp and unmolested like the very first days. The 34mm Rotomatic was the « amateur » recreational version of the professional diver Fifty Fathoms. They both appeared all together in the early fifties catalog.  In a more dressy case, the watch is also powered by the automatic AS 1361N, like the big ones. description: Here is a very nice tropical 69. Wearing a serial in the 29M range, exactly  in the famous « chocolate » range. Being among the early 69, it also inherits a DON bezel from the 321 Speedies. The tropical « chocolate » dial has a very nice mellow and evenly distributed color. title: 1961 Datejust 1603 with bamboo bezel
description: Here is a Datejust you don’t see everyday. Commonly called « Bamboo bezel » because of the pattern of its steel bezel, this rare Datejust was produced only in a very few quantity in the early 60s. Produced only for the Italian market, the bamboo bezel is very different from the fluted or the engine turned bezel. It gives to the watch a totally different look and feel.
